liner.body_md:
## Setlist highlights

- **O is the one**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 5 archived performances [12]

## The recordings

- **mmj2004-06-12.shnf** (recommended): source not stated; 12 songs; 79 min; rated 4.22/5 by 9 [1]. Said about its sound: The recording quality is noted as not being the best; The recording is described as not the greatest sounding but still good; Wind noise and raindrops are audible, especially towards the end of the tape [1][4][6]
- **mmj2004-06-12**: source not stated; 4 songs; 21 min [2]

## Around the show

- The band reportedly made it rain during the performance [3]
- A black sky and rising wind created a creepy atmosphere near the end [4]
- The reviewer attended the Bonnaroo festival and was blown away by the performance [5]
- The storm seemed benevolent, creating a surreal moment for the audience [7]
- Diamond-sized raindrops crashed down while a Tennessee breeze blew during the set [8]
- Bonnaroo officials stated no corporation, including MTV, had bought out the festival [9]
- Jim's voice and the storm made the show memorable for the reviewer [10]
- Minutes of tear-down and shelter time are included after Steam Engine [1]

## Tapers and lineage

- **mmj2004-06-12.shnf**: taped by Mark Lynn; source: DPA (B&K) 4011s > Luminous Monarch XLRs > Lunatec V2 > Luminous Synchestra XLRs > Sonic AD2k+ @ 16/48khz > Tascam DA-P1 [1]
- **mmj2004-06-12**: taped by Joshua Livingston; transferred by Joshua Livingston; source: DAT > CDR > EAC > WAV > SHN [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Buddy Iahn: [My Morning Jacket unveils Bonnaroo 2004 release](https://themusicuniverse.com/my-morning-jacket-unveils-bonnaroo-2004-release/) [13]
